_note: Single source of truth for spike pass criteria. Changing a value is a reviewed edit. Garment clipping is judged by the hard limits under garment_mesh (decided 2026-11-15, docs/decisions/2026-11-15-joe-accepts-fable-review.md); the ray test is reported for information only. Colour tolerances not set yet.

bust_shape._note: V2-08, tops on a female body, measured by pack/bust_shape.py on the exported GLBs at each breast. hollow_below_cm: how far the cloth falls back behind its apex in the 6 cm below it (the tuck under the bust). drop_up_cm and drop_in_cm: how far it falls back 3 cm above and 3 cm towards the centre (a point; 1 cm over 3 cm is a radius of about 4.5 cm, a rounded cup is 6 to 8). Proposed by Claude on 16 Nov 2026 from B, the three synthetic female bodies and the V2-07 pack dress; to be agreed by Joe. The outward drop is reported only: 3 cm out from the apex is the side of the chest.

pack_item_body_as_drawn._note: V3-06, pack items that hide the body under them (the dress; later shoes), run by pack/pack_items.py through mesh_checks.body_as_drawn on the exported GLBs. The app's own garments keep the strict garment_mesh limits (decided 2026-11-16, docs/decisions/2026-11-16-v2-07-joe-decisions.md). visible_body_intersecting_pairs: face pairs between the body as drawn (hidden parts removed) and the item. gap_rays: parallel rays, every ray_spacing_cm over the item's silhouette from each azimuth_step_deg and elevation, where the full body would be seen but the drawn scene shows the inside of the cloth or nothing. Sampling values proposed by Claude and agreed by Joe on 17 Nov 2026. The elevations are the range the app's camera can reach: app/src/viewer.ts limits the polar angle to 0.2 pi to 0.6 pi, i.e. 54 degrees above to 18 degrees below the horizontal. Looking up a skirt from further below is not a view the app can show. push_min_cm (build setting, not a pass limit): pack/pack_items.py pushes any item vertex inside the skin, or closer than this, out to this distance. restore_rings (build setting): body vertices within this many mesh edges of one the cloth does not cover are not hidden either.

shirt._note: V3-03, what makes a shirt a shirt (checked by spike/check_reports.py on the report's collar and placket record, which the generator measures on the finished mesh). A point collar has two points: collar_tip_drop_cm_min is how far the flap must hang below the collar band's top edge at the tips (the drop is 1.5 cm at the front centre and 2 cm round the back, so a collar with no points fails). The placket is the raised strip down the front: at least placket_height_cm_min high, over at least placket_vertices_min vertices. Proposed by Claude on 17 Nov 2026 from the first builds; to be agreed by Joe. shoulder_gap_from_x_cm: the tee's shoulder-gap limits (0.5 cm band mean, 1.0 cm) are applied to a shirt from this distance either side of the centre line outwards instead of from 4 cm, because the collar and its folded flap lie over the base of the neck out to about 8 cm (first build: the shoulders beyond 10 cm measured 0.32 to 0.44 cm, the same as the tee, with the collar in the band at 0.57 cm). Every other limit on the shirt is the tee's.
shirt._note_shading: V3-03 second pass (17 Nov 2026), measured by mesh_checks.shading_look on each shirt GLB as the app gets it. shading_kink_deg_max: over the plain cloth of the torso (clear of the arms, the shoulders, the placket and the collar), the largest turn of the shading normal within 1.5 cm along the cloth. The first shirts measured 40 degrees on B (the tee too), at the bust and navel, where the shell inherits the body template's dense vertex layout and drew the nipples and navel on the cloth ('a skin-tight wrap', Joe); normals averaged over 5 cm measured 17. detail_colour_min_max: the darkest drawn shade in the file (glTF COLOR_0, the collar's lip and the placket edges) must be at most this, so a file exported without the shading fails. Both proposed by Claude; to be agreed by Joe.
